titulo: Mixing bleach with vinegar so it cleans better makes a toxic gas
receta: el que lo hace mal / pilar casa
destinatario: se lo manda alguien a su mamá o a su pareja, el que mezcla bleach con vinagre u otro limpiador 'para que limpie mejor', para decirle que pare
regla_guardable: Bleach alone. Never mixed with vinegar, ammonia or any other cleaner.
fuentes: CDC: Cleaning and Sanitizing with Bleach After an Emergency (stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/44192): 'Never mix bleach with ammonia or any other cleaner.'
CDC: Cleaning and Disinfecting with Bleach (cdc.gov/hygiene/about/cleaning-and-disinfecting-with-bleach.html): follow the label, good ventilation
CDC MMWR (cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/00015111.htm): bleach + acid = chlorine gas; bleach + ammonia products = chloramines

frases.texto: You mix bleach with vinegar so it cleans better.
What it actually makes is a gas.
Vinegar is an acid, and bleach plus an acid releases chlorine gas.
Some cleaners contain ammonia, so check the label. Mixed with bleach, that forms chloramines, another irritating gas.
Chlorine gas can burn the eyes, nose and throat, and cause coughing.
The CDC says it plainly: never mix bleach with ammonia or any other cleaner.
Heads up: the gas comes from the mixing. Use bleach alone, follow the label, and keep the air moving.
Today, one product at a time.
Send this to the friend who mixes everything so it cleans better.
